verdict.rationale: Tavily documents an official MCP server that exposes its search, extract, crawl, map, and research tools. The docs say it works with Claude, ChatGPT, Codex, Cursor, Kiro, VS Code, or any MCP client, and OAuth 2.0 support means no API key has to be hardcoded. A probe confirmed the MCP documentation page exists, and a separate docs MCP server needs no API key or sign-in. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of agents connecting through the MCP server (the only community mention describes wrapping Tavily in a CLI, not using MCP).
